title: Cross-product hooks: where ZIA, ZPA and Client Connector reach into each other
aliases: rule does not match because of another product
risk score in zpa access policy
how do these products fit together

prose.text: The products are configured separately, but a field or decision in one often depends on state in another, and a question framed around one product can resolve in another. This subject maps those hooks by direction and points at where each is held.

checks.do: For an SSL/TLS rule that does not list or match a Private Access segment: whether Source IP Anchor is enabled on the segment.
For a TRUSTED_NETWORK access condition that never matches: whether Send Trusted Network Result to ZPA is on in the user's active forwarding profile.
For a user who reaches no Private Access application: the user's (and device group's) Private Access entitlement before any access rule.
For a risk-score access rule that does not fire for a user: the user's current risk score level, including Unknown.
For DLP, Sandbox, malware or Cloud App Control misses on HTTPS: whether the traffic matched a Do Not Inspect rule.
For certificate errors on one platform only: the Install Zscaler SSL Certificate setting of that platform's app profile, and the macOS version.
For a URL newly blocked with no rule change: whether ATP's AI/ML tools moved it into a Botnet or Phishing category.
For a change that took effect in one product and not the other: whether the Internet & SaaS change was activated.

risk-score-source.statement: Private Access access policy has a Risk Scores criterion: user risk scores from a risk source, Internet & SaaS being the vendor's example.

quotes: Risk Scores: User risk scores from a risk source (e.g., Internet & SaaS).

risk-score-without-history.title: Which risk level a user with no Internet & SaaS risk score matches, and what feeds the score
risk-score-without-history.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "the user must have enough ZIA activity for a risk score to exist. Users with no ZIA history get a default-low score — the rule never fires for them", and the score draws on Page Risk, ATP detections and Suspicious Content Protection. Internet & SaaS assigns users a risk score based on their browsing activities, grouped into levels whose default ranges start with Low at 0 to 29 (zia.url-filtering.criteria:user-risk-score-levels). Still open: whether a user without a score matches UNKNOWN or LOW in a Private Access rule (the operand values include both, zpa.policy.conditions:risk-factor-entry), and whether Page Risk, ATP or Suspicious Content Protection contribute.
